prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1491; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a low-speed collision in a shopping center parking lot, with the claimant reporting neck and back strain and stating they are not represented by an attorney.
Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver involved is listed as a named driver, with coverage in force at the time of loss.
Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene and notes the other driver's statement matches the claimant's account.
Entry 4: Spoke with two witnesses who independently describe the backing vehicle striking the claimant's car, and both confirm the sequence of events as reported.
Entry 5: Received photos of the scene and both vehicles; the visible damage is mostly consistent with the described impact and the points of contact line up.
Entry 6: Checked prior claim history and found no earlier damage recorded on this vehicle, and no earlier claims involving the same body area for the claimant.
Entry 7: Claimant gave a recorded statement and repeated the same account of the collision that was given at first notice of loss and in the follow-up call.
Entry 8: Medical records show the diagnosis of neck and back strain is a typical result of this kind of impact, with the force described in the file being a reasonable match.
Entry 9: Treatment followed a usual course of physical therapy and medication, with visit frequency tapering as the claimant reported steady improvement.
Entry 10: Reviewed the damage estimate and the repair records; nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start date, and no prior loss is indicated.
Entry 11: Claim assessed as consistent with the reported loss and moving toward resolution, pending final treatment summary from the treating provider.
